claims.claim: Hong Kong should tighten rent control on subdivided units in stages, not with a hard cap.
The first step should be to build a tenancy register and survey data.
The second step should be to give tenants security of tenure.
The third step should be to add a published band on initial rents.
About 110,000 households live in subdivided units and pay a 15-25% premium per square foot compared with ordinary flats.
Subdivided unit tenants are mostly new arrivals, single parents, and people waiting for public housing.
The 2021 ordinance limits rent increases inside a tenancy but does not cap the initial rent.
After 2021, rents in subdivided units grew more slowly than general rents, but the share of income spent on rent rose from 31% to 34%.
The landlords' association says a hard cap is confiscatory and members will leave the business if returns fall below mortgage cost.
The landlords' submission lacks data on members' real margins and its cost figures come from a self-reported survey with a 34% response rate.
A working paper estimates that hard caps on rent levels remove roughly 3 to 5 percent of stock for every 10 percent rent cut, harming poor households.
Controls that only limit increases inside tenancies have small or null effects on stock, and stock rose from 107,300 in 2021 to 111,200 in 2025.
An NGO survey of 440 households found that 61 percent would trade a rent rise for three years of security of tenure.
The NGO report says rent caps treat the price symptom of a quantity problem and inspection effort is better spent on fire and ventilation.
Rent control cannot fix a waiting time of around five and a half years for public housing.
A draft internal minute says inspection covers under 6 percent of the stock each year and a band on initial rents needs a certifiable register taking 40 to 60 staff-years to build.
If tenants must complain to enforce the rule, the newest arrivals and those with no written agreement will be missed first.
Counsel thinks a hard cap on initial rents would likely lead to compensation claims on property rights, while the 2021 style is on firmer legal ground but leaves initial rent unregulated.
A published, indexed band is more legally defensible but requires a survey system that does not exist yet.
If the register cannot be built, the band should wait and not be passed as an empty rule.
